Notable changes to the structure of the [[Players Committee]] (PC): its teams, committees and chart.

* '''2002–2003.''' Besides the Advocates, the early swccgpc.com had a Staff Writer, Duane Bruun (Shadow 47),<ref name="pc-jan03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030612020737/http://swccgpc.com:80/Archives/january03archives.htm January 03 Updates], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 June 2003.</ref><ref name="pc-bruun02">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030613110815/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/duane2002yearend.htm The State Of SWCCG], Duane Bruun (PC Staff Writer), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 June 2003.</ref> and a Championship Circuit Assistant, [[Nick Kolnik]] (April 2003).<ref name="pc-apr03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030810085606/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/april03archives.htm April 03 Updates], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 10 August 2003.</ref> The Advocate Council page of April 2003 gives short biographies and names the subcommittees: [[Jim Colson]] ("40 something", Huntsville, Alabama), Shadow Squadron Leader; [[Andrew Howard]] (19, Chicago), in charge of the Classic Format Subcommittee; [[Eric Olson]] (26, Chicago), manager of the Q&A Subcommittee that proofread the virtual cards; [[Josh Radke]] (23, Bristol, Connecticut); [[Jason Robinette]] (31, New York), head of the Young Jedi Design Subcommittee; and [[Doug Taylor]] (37, Seattle), head of the Proofreading and Public Relations subcommittees and liaison with ''Scrye'' magazine.<ref name="pc-council03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030418002012/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/council.htm Advocate Council] (April 2003), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 18 April 2003.</ref> In May 2003 the site called [[Duane Bruun]] both PC Staff Writer and Squadron Member.<ref name="pc-may03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/may03archives.htm May Updates], swccgpc.com (16 and 21 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20031229115404/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/may03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Late 2002.''' Looking ahead to 2003, the PC announces an exclusive strategic partnership with [[DeckTech|Decktech Inc.]]; the DPC Championship Series, co-sponsored by Decktech and the PC, is to give players the first chance to qualify for Worlds and win cash at the same events. Volunteers are sought to run [[Young Jedi]] and [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game|Jedi Knights]] events at all major conventions in 2003.<ref name="pc-road03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003; SWCCG Player's Committee Announces Strategic Partnership], swccgpc.com (undated, late 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620161313/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''13 December 2002.''' The Road to Worlds announcement, posted on the PC forum by Tournament Support Advocate [[Andrew Howard]], sets out the four tiers of the 2003 Championship Circuit. Tier 1, the State, National and Provincial Championships (April–June), is run by local volunteers and Squadron Members, costs the director $25, has a suggested $5 entry and plays 6–8 games of Swiss with a top-2 final, the winner qualifying for Day 2 of Worlds. Tier 2, the Open Qualifiers (March–September; 5–8 in North America and 3 internationally), is run by Squadron Members, costs the director $50, has a suggested $10 entry and plays 8 games of Swiss with a top-4 playoff, the top 2 qualifying. Tier 3, the DPC Championship Series (at least 6 events, including Origins, Gen Con, Essen and the European Championships), is run by Player Advocates and/or Squadron Members, with a required $20 entry split among the top 4. Tier 4, the World Championships, is run by the Player Advocates. Special events include Grand Slams for SWCCG, Young Jedi and Jedi Knights and [[Classic]] format events, with prizes such as uncut sheets, trophies and Virtual Card sets. The announcement calls the PC "the first player run organization to have full control over the future of a CCG" and the DPCs "the first pro series for SWCCG".<ref name="pcf-426-6397">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=6397#6397 Player's Committee Outlines Road to Worlds 2003], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318152757/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=6397%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''January 2003.''' Posts on the PC forum are signed by a member of a Jedi Knights Subcommittee (posting as Bubba Joe).<ref name="pcf-525-9349">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=9349#9349 Do People want events for Jedi Knights at Cons this year?], Bubba Joe, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050227224220/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=13842%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''13 March 2003.''' [[Nick Kolnik]] explains on the forum that for the 2003 Championship Circuit, State Championships replaced Regionals as qualifiers, having been judged the better qualifier format.<ref name="pcf-1120-20337">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=20337#20337 Regions], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 March 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041121022250/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=20327%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''March 2003.''' The Classic Format Subcommittee revises the rules of the [[Classic]] format, which becomes an official format for all sanctioned events, including the Championship Circuit; the subcommittee keeps its ban list under continuing review.<ref name="pc-classic0331">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/classicnews03312003.htm Classic Format Contest Results are In!], swccgpc.com (31 March 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030824053912/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/classicnews03312003.htm Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''June 2003.''' Because Decipher was changing its tournament and ranking software, the PC forms a tournament-software subcommittee with [[Eric Olson]] and [[Andrew Howard]] as project managers; meanwhile tournament directors are asked to register a credit card with Decipher.<ref name="pc-tourchg">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809102648/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/tournamentchanges06182003.htm Upcoming Changes to Decipher's Tournament Software; How does it affect you?], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref>
* '''March 2004.''' [[Jim Colson]] describes the PC's stock of donated product. Decipher had shipped about five tons of product to a warehouse in Colorado owned by [[Scott Gaeta]], whom Colson counted as the half of the two and a half original advocates living in Colorado; when they were no longer advocates, the stock was moved to a warehouse in Alabama that Colson managed, the move subsidized in part by [[Warren Holland]]. About half of the inventory was [[Young Jedi]] and [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game|Jedi Knights]] product; the PC never received a box of [[Reflections]] I, II or III or any Death Star II boosters. Uncut sheets were only given out as prizes, while booster boxes were used for prizes, sold for income or sent out as convention support. The PC webstore was not owned by the PC but by Universal Cards, which had bought product from the PC about a year before; the PC received a small commission on sales through it.<ref name="pcf-2324-41900">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=41900#41900 Would a 'Collecting SWCCG' group of articles be welcomed?], Jim Colson (ShadowLeader), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 March 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041030164316/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=41852%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''April 2004.''' Players on the PC forum criticise the Committee's visibility. [[Garrett Larson]] writes that after Virtual Set 5 the advocates became nearly invisible, that Andrew Howard had been the most visible figure, and that [[Mitch Velasco]] took over when Howard left;<ref name="pcf-3180-44980">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44980#44980 SWCCG worlds and more], deadbody, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> a player posting as Darth Hoth writes that traffic to swccgpc.com had been falling since Virtual Set 4 (January 2003), that no advocates had been seen on the forum since Howard stepped down, and that the main page had last been updated two months before.<ref name="pcf-3180-44998">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44998#44998 SWCCG worlds and more], Darth Hoth, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''19 April – 19 May 2004.''' The Flight Leader program is announced on 19 April 2004, and the first Flight Leaders are named on 19 May 2004; [[Josh Radke]] becomes the first Kashyyyk Flight Leader.<ref name="pc-int0406">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040602195521/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news (May 2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 2 June 2004.</ref> The Shadow Squadron page of June 2004 lists the regions and their Flight Leaders (see [[SWCCG regions]]).<ref name="pc-vol04">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040604020531/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/volunteers.htm Shadow Squadron (volunteers by region)] (June 2004), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 4 June 2004.</ref>
* '''June 2004.''' Two new Player Advocates join: [[Kevin Brownell]] as Marketing & Player Relations PA, to keep the community up to date on events and news, publish articles, features and interviews, and act as liaison between the players and the PC; and [[Nick Kolnik]] as Marketing & Tournaments PA, to market tournaments, keep players informed of tournament news and support the Tournaments PA.<ref name="webgroup" /> A WebGroup is formed to coordinate the PC website: webmaster Keith Allen, with [[Jason Robinette]], [[David Destefanis]], John Davis, [[Kevin Brownell]] and [[Nick Kolnik]].<ref name="webgroup">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040603214022/http://www.swccgpc.com/News/NewAdvocates.htm New Advocates! Not 1 but 2!], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 3 June 2004)</ref> Forum posters were already congratulating Brownell and Kolnik as the two new advocates on 24 May 2004, after the announcement on the main site, and looked forward to the new "webgroup".<ref name="pcf-3349-46706">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46706#46706 Congrats to the new Advocates!], Jedi K, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212439/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46930%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-3349-46715">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46715#46715 Congrats to the new Advocates!], Rustan Sharer, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212439/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46930%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''15 July 2005.''' Scott Lingrell posts a recap of player requests and the PC's answers: no unified ratings system yet; an "avoid the sledgehammer" approach to slowing the game, with cards such as the Shocks in [[Virtual Set 10]]; no plan for a Coruscant (V) set; the main page now updated two to three times a week; the old collecting thread lost; Shadow Squadron membership being updated; Virtual Sets 1–9 to be corrected that week; a deckbuilder on Essential SW that can export to Holotable; the World Wide Ladder league; card lists in the Outpost forum with [[Chuck Sonnenburg|Sonn]]; new articles by [[Mike Tomashewski|Shewski]] and [[Jacob Taylor]]; and a rules update expected before Worlds.<ref name="pcf-6375-88430">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=88430#88430 A Recap and more questions.], Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 July 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618064056/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=89004 Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''May 2006.''' The Shadow Squadron is the PC's marketing arm. A Proofreading Subcommittee and a Public Relations Subcommittee are headed by [[Doug Taylor]], and a Young Jedi Design Subcommittee by [[Jason Robinette]].<ref name="adv2006">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221233/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=Content&pa=showpage&pid=3 Advocates], swccgpc.com Content pid=3 (published 1 May 2006; Wayback, 17 June 2006)</ref> On 23 May 2006 the PC asks for volunteers for a Writing Team (one monthly article or deck submission), a Graphic Designer (promotional flyers and more) and an Intern (for college credit), with [[Scott Lingrell]] as the contact.<ref name="pc-sid8">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8 Volunteers Needed], swccgpc.com (23 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617220108/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8 Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''6 May 2006.''' Carr writes that for the previous four months the PC had been trying to stay solvent and keep the burden of future Worlds on players as small as possible while still giving prizes worth travelling for, and explains why Worlds is moving away from GenCon: GenCon charged $1.50 per player per hour in its gaming area, players needed a $65–75 pass, and multi-day events could no longer have a single entry fee.<ref name="pcf-9457-135624">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=135624#135624 Road to Worlds 2006], Michael Carr (mc9457), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618072946/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138185&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref>

Regional Flight Leaders (tournament contacts) and Key Volunteers who lead teams are listed beside the Advocate Council: Website Admin, Moderators, Watto's Cube Team, Player Created Card Team, Proofreading, Graphic Design, Rules Moderators, Competitive Balance Team, Star Wars Information Pool and Tournament Committee.<ref name="vol2008">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080925101022/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/volunteer/ Volunteer], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 25 September 2008)</ref>
* '''September 2008.''' Members who have paid for premium memberships through PayPal, including a six-month level, report receiving a custom avatar but not yet access to the premium forums;<ref name="pcf-22212-335037">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=335037#335037 Going premium], citizenSwanky, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 September 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080916195925/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=335040&sid=d06ad6437369bcd26a837f9f518a057c Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-22212-336098">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=336098#336098 Going premium], NateA, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 September 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080916195925/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=335040&sid=d06ad6437369bcd26a837f9f518a057c Internet Archive]</ref> Lingrell asks Evan to look into the user groups.<ref name="pcf-22212-335040">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=335040#335040 Going premium], Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 September 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080916195925/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=335040&sid=d06ad6437369bcd26a837f9f518a057c Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''July 2009.''' The Volunteer page, now on starwarsccg.org, adds a Premium Member Admin and announces two Flight Leaders per region.<ref name="vol2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102812/http://www.starwarsccg.org/volunteer/ Volunteer], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref>
* '''June 2018.''' The PC takes over [[GEMP]] from its creator, [[Troy Biesterfeld]], and invites applications for a development team. A new [[Multimedia and Special Projects Advocate]] leads the team.<ref name="gemp2018">[https://web.archive.org/web/20201128163934/https://www.starwarsccg.org/gemp-announcements-request-for-applications-for-new-team/ GEMP Announcements &amp; Request for Applications for New Team], starwarsccg.org (7 June 2018; Wayback, 28 November 2020)</ref>
* '''July 2018.''' Design opens applications for the Design and Development team and the Player Card Development team.<ref name="dd2018">[https://web.archive.org/web/20200927002833/https://www.starwarsccg.org/call-for-applications-dd-team-and-player-card-dev-team/ Call for Applications &ndash; D&amp;D Team and Player Card Dev Team], starwarsccg.org (18 July 2018; Wayback, 27 September 2020)</ref>
* '''December 2020.''' The Jawa Council ([[Kendall Halman]], [[Eric Hunter]] and [[Bill Kafer]]) updates the banned list of the Jawa Format, an alternative format on GEMP.<ref name="jawa">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210125020218/https://www.starwarsccg.org/jawa-format-banned-list-updated/ Jawa Format Banned List Updated!], starwarsccg.org (19 December 2020; Wayback, 25 January 2021)</ref>
* '''January 2021.''' The PC publishes an organization chart under About Us, to be updated every couple of months.<ref name="orgpost">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210130223738/https://www.starwarsccg.org/players-committee-org-chart-published/ Players Committee Org Chart Published!], starwarsccg.org (30 January 2021)</ref> The chart of 14 February 2021 shows Legal and PC Store Manager beside the Lead Advocate.<ref name="oc2021feb">[https://web.archive.org/web/20210214073243/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.jpg PC organization chart], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 14 February 2021)</ref>
* '''March 2021.''' The Competitive Balance Team is announced: 11 members chaired by [[Jarad Konsker]], including several advocates.<ref name="cbt">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/meet-the-competitive-balance-team/ Meet the Competitive Balance Team], starwarsccg.org (25 March 2021)</ref>
* '''July 2021.''' A redesigned chart groups the volunteer teams under labeled sub-teams: GEMP Slicers, Proofing, Playtesting, Player Card Development, Graphics, Competitive Balance Team and Design &amp; Development.<ref name="oc2021pdf" />
* '''May 2024.''' The Technology team moves under the [[Rules Advocate]], and the new [[Production Advocate]] heads Player Card Development and Graphics. The Outreach Team, Stream Team, Decklist Scribe Team and Design Pods are new to the chart.<ref name="oc2024">PC organization chart PDF (created 6 May 2024), [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010210152/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf archived PDF]</ref>
